convertedTask.title: Zero-Infrastructure Web Deployment with AWS App Runner
convertedTask.goal: Goal: Deploy a web application directly from a container image with built-in auto-scaling, SSL/TLS certificates, and zero container orchestration setup.

concepts.title: AWS App Runner Overview
concepts.body: Fully managed service for deploying containerized web applications directly without managing VPCs, load balancers, domain certificates, or orchestrators.

concepts.title: App Runner vs ECS / EKS
concepts.body: App Runner: Simplest web app deployment with zero VPC/ELB configuration. ECS / EKS: Full custom networking, daemonsets, sidecars, and cluster control.

concepts.title: Automatic Concurrency Scaling
concepts.body: Scales active container instances automatically based on real-time concurrent HTTP request volume per instance.

concepts.title: Automatic HTTPS Domain Provisioning
concepts.body: App Runner automatically generates a public HTTPS URL and manages SSL/TLS certificate renewals out of the box.

concepts.title: App Runner vs ECS vs EKS Decision Matrix
concepts.body: FeatureAWS App RunnerAmazon ECS (Fargate)Amazon EKS (Kubernetes)Primary focusWeb apps & APIsMicroservices & background tasksComplex Kubernetes workloadsInfrastructure setupZero (No VPC / ELB needed)Low (Task defs & service setup)High (K8s manifests & control plane)Load balancerAuto-provisioned HTTPSManual ALB / NLB attachmentManual Ingress / ALB ControllerAuto scaling metricConcurrent HTTP requestsCPU / Memory / Custom CloudWatchHorizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA)Custom networkingOptional VPC ConnectorFull VPC / Subnet controlFull VPC / CNI Plugin control

convertedTask.whyItMatters: This matters because SAA-C03 tests when to pick App Runner (simplest web app deployment with zero VPC/ELB management) vs. ECS/EKS (full custom networking, sidecars, and cluster control).
convertedTask.costWarning: Low cost: App Runner charges $0.007/GB-hour for memory and $0.064/vCPU-hour during active requests. Delete the App Runner service immediately after completing your practice lab.

consoleSteps.title: Set up the lab user and permissions

instructions.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console.
Use an IAM user or role (do not use the root user).
For a personal learning account, AdministratorAccess is acceptable while practising.
For least privilege, use the grouped permissions below.

consoleSteps.note: Identity check: sts:GetCallerIdentity App Runner permissions: apprunner:CreateService, apprunner:DescribeService, apprunner:ListServices Cleanup: apprunner:DeleteService
consoleSteps.warning: Do not leave broad admin access or long-term access keys in real company accounts.

consoleSteps.title: Open AWS App Runner Console

instructions.text: Open AWS App Runner.
Choose Region us-east-1.
Choose Create an App Runner service.

consoleSteps.note: App Runner provides a single wizard to deploy web applications from source code or container images.

consoleSteps.title: Configure Source Container Image

instructions.text: Under Repository type, select Container registry.
Select Public ECR (or Private ECR).
Enter Container image URI: public.ecr.aws/docker/library/nginx:latest.
Under Deployment trigger, select Manual.
Choose Next.

consoleSteps.note: App Runner can also connect directly to GitHub repositories for automatic build-and-deploy pipelines.

consoleSteps.title: Configure Service and Instance Settings

instructions.text: Set Service name to saa-apprunner-web-service.
Set Port to 80.
Under Virtual CPU and memory, select 1 vCPU and 2 GB memory.
Keep Environment variables blank for default NGINX testing.

consoleSteps.note: App Runner automatically routes incoming HTTP traffic to the specified container port.

consoleSteps.title: Configure Concurrency Auto Scaling Rules

instructions.text: Under Auto scaling, keep Default configuration selected (Max concurrency: 100 requests/instance, Min size: 1, Max size: 25).
Under Health check, set Path to / and Protocol to HTTP.
Choose Next -> Review settings -> Choose Create & deploy.

consoleSteps.note: App Runner scales instance count based on real-time HTTP request concurrency per instance.

consoleSteps.title: Verify Automatic HTTPS Domain and CloudWatch Logs

instructions.text: Wait 2–3 minutes for service status to transition to Running.
Locate the Default domain URL (e.g. https://xxxxxx.us-east-1.awsapprunner.com).
Click the link to open the public HTTPS URL in your browser.
Confirm the NGINX welcome page loads over a valid SSL certificate.
Select Logs tab to inspect real-time CloudWatch application logs.

consoleSteps.note: App Runner handles public DNS records, HTTPS certificate renewals, and CloudWatch log streaming automatically.

consoleSteps.title: Tear down App Runner resources

instructions.text: Select service saa-apprunner-web-service -> Click Actions -> Choose Delete.
Type the service name to confirm and click Delete.

consoleSteps.warning: Delete the App Runner service to stop memory provisioned charges.

cheatSheet.title: AWS App Runner Overview
cheatSheet.body: Fully managed zero-infrastructure service for deploying web applications and APIs directly from container images or source repositories.

cheatSheet.title: When to Choose App Runner
cheatSheet.body: Choose App Runner for simple web apps when you want zero VPC, zero ALB, zero SSL, and zero cluster management.

cheatSheet.title: When to Choose ECS / EKS
cheatSheet.body: Choose ECS or EKS when you need custom VPC networking, sidecar containers, mesh routing, daemonsets, or non-HTTP protocols.

troubleshooting.title: App Runner Service Deployment Pending
troubleshooting.body: Check container port settings. Ensure the container exposes the exact HTTP port specified in the App Runner configuration (Port 80).

examTraps.title: App Runner vs Elastic Beanstalk
examTraps.body: App Runner is container-native with zero infrastructure management. Beanstalk provisions underlying EC2 instances, Auto Scaling groups, and ALBs into your VPC.

examTips.text: SAA-C03: Master AWS App Runner concepts and container orchestration patterns in AWS App Runner.
